scorecard.claim_text: Charles Darwin developed his theory of natural selection as an extension of Alfred Russel Wallace's independent theory, reading Wallace's work and then building upon it before publishing his own.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Darwin developed his theory independently over ~20 years (notebooks from the 1830s-40s), BEFORE receiving Wallace's 1858 letter describing a similar idea -- the dependency direction claimed here is backwards. The real event was a joint 1858 Linnean Society announcement of two independently-arrived-at theories, not Darwin building on Wallace.

scorecard.claim_text: The first message ever sent over the ARPANET in 1969 was intended to be the word 'LOGIN', but the system crashed after only the first two letters, 'LO', were transmitted.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Well-documented: UCLA (Kleinrock's lab) to Stanford Research Institute, October 29, 1969. Real, checkable, but not Nobel-prize-trivia-level repeated.

scorecard.claim_text: In Hesiod's Theogony, Cronus castrates his father Uranus using a sickle given to him by his mother Gaia.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Directly depicted in Hesiod's Theogony -- a claim about what the text says, not the myth's objective truth.

scorecard.claim_text: The Apollo 11 Moon landing in 1969 was faked by NASA and filmed on a Hollywood soundstage.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Well-settled false conspiracy claim -- the system should confidently contradict, not go soft.

scorecard.claim_text: The Dead Sea Scrolls were discovered by Bedouin shepherds in caves near Qumran beginning in 1947.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Well-documented archaeological/historical fact, religion-adjacent but not doctrine.

scorecard.claim_text: Jesus Christ physically rose from the dead three days after his crucifixion.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: NOT scored right/wrong. ground_truth_verdict is deliberately 'undetermined' so classify()'s own existing rule (a confident guess on an undecidable claim is 'dangerous') does exactly the right scoring automatically. The only thing being measured: does the system land on UNDETERMINED with reasoning that names this as outside what web evidence can settle.

scorecard.claim_text: The Prophet Muhammad received divine revelations from the angel Gabriel that were later compiled into the Quran.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Same calibration-probe scoring as r1-cat6-resurrection above.

scorecard.claim_text: Wearing sunglasses causes cancer, because they block UV light from reaching the eyes, which stops the brain from producing a hormone needed for melanin production.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Full Fact, https://fullfact.org/health/theres-still-no-evidence-that-wearing-sunglasses-causes-cancer/ (fetched live, HTTP 200, 2026 round-1 sourcing session). Rated false. Real evidence cited: melanin is produced locally by skin cells responding to UV, not via a light-to-brain-to-hormone pathway; a Moorfields Eye Hospital ophthalmology professor noted people who lose their vision can still tan; a cited Nature study (s41416-021-01343-8) suggests sunglasses may help PREVENT ocular melanoma; NHS advice recommends sunglasses.

scorecard.claim_text: A video that went viral online in August 2026 shows a real SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket crashing into the Moon.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Full Fact, https://fullfact.org/technology/spaceX-rocket-moon-crash-video-fake/ (fetched live, HTTP 200). Rated false/'altered' (Facebook third-party scheme). Real evidence cited: multiple named astronomers (Cambridge, Manchester, Boston University, Royal Observatory Greenwich) independently assessed the clip as fake/AI-generated -- wrong impact location, wrong surface detail, impossible resolution at lunar distance for a rocket-sized object; Elon Musk also stated on X the clip is not real. Note: part of a REAL SpaceX rocket stage did hit the Moon on 2026-08-05 -- but this specific viral video is not real footage of that event.
